title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) to measure the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic verifier+repair step (G→V→R) before applying LLM‑generated network configuration suggestions. Using a deterministic task generator and validator we selected K=200 tasks by a reproducible SHA‑256 sorting rule and used a single shared generator output per task so both arms evaluated the identical candidate. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair path was never invoked. We release the full execution and scoring artifacts for replay (notable fingerprints: raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13..., task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7..., master prompt provenance at provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). We interpret the result as a ceiling/null outcome for the tested model/validator/task sampling regime and discuss implications for designing future failure‑rich evaluations.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation is a high‑value NetOps objective but carries risk: incorrect device commands can cause reachability regressions, service disruption, or security exposure. Generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipelines—where a generative LLM proposes configuration changes, a deterministic verifier checks them against formalised workflow and safety constraints, and a repairer attempts corrections—are widely advocated to mitigate those risks. However, rigorous, preregistered causal evidence quantifying the verifier’s marginal utility under reproducible sampling contracts is sparse. We therefore preregistered a paired experiment (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) whose confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (the per‑task difference in binary validator pass rate when the same generated candidate is accepted directly vs passed through verify→repair). Key execution constraints were preregistered and archived (preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...); the autonomous run archived every provider call, candidate, validator trace, and hashed artifact (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...).

Research question. Does inserting a deterministic verify→repair stage reduce the rate of regression‑causing changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly when the same generated candidate is evaluated in both arms?

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired confirmatory run and analysis that isolates verifier marginality on fixed generator outputs. (2) An artifact‑grounded report of a reproducible ceiling/null outcome (no discordant pairs observed). (3) Operational recommendations and reproducibility artifacts needed to design future failure‑rich assessments.
sections.related_work: Work on LLM‑assisted NetOps emphasises generate–validate–repair architectures, tool‑orchestration, and verifier‑guided workflows (recent benchmarks and position papers such as Cornetto and concurrent work on verifiable model translation/TypoNet and self‑evolving verifiers). Surveys on LLMs for NetOps and AIOps emphasise that operational reliability typically depends more on surrounding machinery (validators, canary trials, rollback) than on model fluency alone. Our study differs: we provide a preregistered paired causal estimate of a verifier+repair module’s marginal effect under a deterministic, artifact‑archived execution contract. All cited prior works used in framing and positioning are verified and archived among the run’s evidence records (see cited_record_ids list).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the experimental protocol before observing outcomes (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...). The primary confirmatory test is the paired binary comparison of validator passes (McNemar exact two‑sided), supplemented by a paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) to form a percentile CI for the paired difference.

Deterministic task selection. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and filtered to intents covered by the preregistered deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). To avoid human selection bias, the manifest applied a deterministic selection rule: compute SHA‑256(intent_string), sort ascending, and select the first K=200 unique tasks. The manifest and its SHA‑256 are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). Each task includes a machine‑readable intent, initial and expected final state, difficulty metadata, and workflow constraints.

Shared initial generation and arm semantics. For each task a single shared generator call (shared_initial_generation) produced candidate_c which both arms evaluated. Baseline: candidate_c is accepted and scored post‑apply by the validator. Guarded: candidate_c is sent to the verifier prior to apply; if violations are detected, at most one repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1) is allowed to produce a repaired candidate; the repaired candidate is revalidated. The shared‑initial design isolates the verifier’s marginal effect on fixed candidates but prevents adaptive regeneration in response to validator feedback (this design decision was preregistered and is discussed below as it constrains interpretation).

Models, tooling, and capture. Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13...). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (verifier encodes workflow policies: protected_interfaces, must_be_down_for_fields, final group minima, etc.). All provider call traces, responses, and scoring JSONs were archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json, execution/responses/*.txt, execution/scoring/*.json). Key fingerprints: raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256 = 79c91155..., and provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e....

Statistical preface to degenerate outcomes. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate (≈0.20). In paired designs, if no discordant pairs are observed (n10=n01=0) then the paired difference is exactly 0.00, the exact McNemar test yields p=1.00, and the empirical paired bootstrap without additional assumptions reproduces a degenerate percentile CI [0.00,0.00]. We executed the planned bootstrap (10,000 replicates; seed=1729) and report that degenerate CI. This is the correct descriptive inference given the observed concordant outcomes.
sections.results:
Execution provenance and accounting. Planned episodes: 400 (two arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (one shared initial generation per task; no repair calls were invoked). No provider or infrastructure failures affected the scientific run. Full provenance artifacts and hashes are archived for replay: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4..., execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7..., and provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e.... Deterministic reconciliation confirms consistent episode accounting and absence of cross‑condition cache reuse (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json archived).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). Complete paired counts: complete_pairs = 200. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The repair pathway was never invoked: repair_applied=false appears in every execution/scoring/*.json for guarded episodes.

Representative diagnostics and task metadata. Each scoring JSON records structured validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot, difficulty metadata). Example artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 3055f874...), execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 95bddd4f...), and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = d10b415a...). The per‑task difficulty metadata and workflow constraints for all K=200 tasks are preserved in execution/scoring/*.json; investigators can deterministically aggregate the distribution of difficulty levels and validator coverage by replaying those JSONs (artifact locations and hashes are provided in the archive).

Why no repairs occurred (artifact‑grounded account). Three artifact‑grounded factors explain the degenerate outcome: (1) inclusion rule bias — tasks were included only if the preregistered validator reported coverage for the intent class, which preferentially selects intents the validator can check; (2) generator strength — the requested model (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that, for these validator‑covered intents, satisfied workflow constraints as encoded in the task payloads (normalized_response == reference for all archived candidates); (3) shared_initial_generation — because both arms evaluated the identical candidate, the guard condition could only affect outcome if the candidate failed validation and triggered repair. All three factors are evident in the archived artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json and model/provider traces) and together explain the ceiling/null result.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and bounded claims. The observed ceiling/null outcome (no discordant pairs) is an empirical fact under the preregistered, archived contract: with the selected generator, validator coverage filter, and shared_initial design, initial candidates satisfied the validator in every selected task. This run therefore provides no evidence that the verifier+repair step improves the binary validator pass rate for the tested model/task/validator regime. It does not imply that verifiers are unnecessary in general; rather, it exposes that a confirmatory paired design will be uninformative when the baseline error rate within the sampled population is effectively zero.

Design implications for future evaluations (artifact‑grounded recommendations). To produce informative, nondegenerate confirmatory estimates of verifier utility we recommend (and archive artifacts to support): (A) sampling or constructing failure‑rich task distributions (include historical misconfigurations or adversarial boundary cases) so baseline error prevalence is nonzero; (B) evaluating multiple generator strengths (including weaker models) so the generator baseline error regime broadens; (C) adopting an interactive estimator where generator regeneration is permitted in response to verifier feedback (closed‑loop estimand) if the goal is end‑to‑end improvement; and (D) publishing per‑task validator coverage and difficulty aggregates alongside paired counts. The execution archive deliberately retained per‑task difficulty and validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) to enable precisely these follow‑up studies and deterministic resampling.

Statistical note on degenerate bootstrap and inference. When every observed pair is concordant the empirical paired distribution contains no variation in the paired difference and the nonparametric bootstrap reproduces the same point mass; reporting the degenerate percentile CI [0.00,0.00] and McNemar p=1.00 correctly characterises the data. The preregistered power calculation (targeting baseline≈0.20) therefore becomes irrelevant post hoc; results must be interpreted descriptively for the tested regime.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: shared_initial_generation isolates verifier marginality but prevents generator adaptation; we archived provider calls and model responses so others can re‑run an alternative adaptive design. Construct validity: the binary validator verdict depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 coverage; if important regression modes lie outside that validator’s rule set, the binary outcome conflates ‘validator pass’ with true production safety. External validity: single requested_model (gpt-5-mini) and the validator‑coverage inclusion rule constrain generalisability to broader models and production intent distributions. Conclusion validity: observed ceiling undermines preregistered power assumptions; our analysis reports exact paired counts and bootstrap CI without overinterpreting p‑values.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully artifact‑archived paired evaluation measuring the verifier+repair marginal effect on fixed LLM candidates. Under the preregistered deterministic inclusion rule and requested model (gpt-5-mini), all shared generator outputs passed the deterministic validator both when accepted directly and when passed through verify→repair: baseline = 200/200; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. Repairs were never applied. This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (notable fingerprints listed above) and should be read as a regime‑specific outcome: it does not generalize to failure‑rich or production distributions. Future confirmatory work should intentionally sample failure‑rich tasks, vary generator strengths, or adopt interactive closed‑loop estimands. All execution artifacts, validator traces, and the exact initial master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...) are released for replay and audit to support cumulative evaluation in the NetOps domain.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Synthetic deterministic task pool and the preregistered inclusion rule (validator coverage required) bias the confirmed sample toward intents the validator already covers and limit external validity to production intent distributions that contain historical or adversarial misconfigurations.
Construct validity is tied to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator coverage gaps mean a validator pass may not equal production safety for unmodelled regression modes.

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes generator outputs across arms and prevents generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; inference is descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
